rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Fission** splits a heavy nucleus: ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n + ~200 MeV, with the freed neutrons sustaining a **chain reaction** (controlled in reactors by moderators and control rods). **Fusion** joins light nuclei: ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV, but demands ~10⁸ K to overcome Coulomb repulsion — the engine of the Sun.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n + ~200 MeV - ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV - E = Δmc²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Criticality: Chain reaction self-sustains when each fission causes exactly one more fission (k = 1). k < 1 subcritical, k > 1 supercritical.  ·  Fusion Temperature: ~10⁸ K needed — much hotter than sun's core (~1.5×10⁷ K) because terrestrial fusion uses D-T (easier than p-p).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion combines light nuclei; both release energy because the binding energy per nucleon increases toward iron."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The Sun*** — hydrogen fusion at ~10⁸ K in the core; the energy of stars is thermonuclear.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Fission = split (heavy), fusion = join (light)** — both climb toward the iron peak.  ·  **Fusion beats fission per kilogram** — but needs ~10⁸ K, which is why reactors use fission.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Splitting and Joining for Energy Both routes to nuclear energy walk up the binding-energy curve toward iron: **fission** splits a heavy nucleus, **fusion** joins light ones. Each gram of fuel converts milligrams of mass into energy millions of times beyond any chemical reaction.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022) ### 2.1 Nuclear fission A heavy nucleus (A > 200) absorbs a neutron and splits into two medium nuclei plus neutrons and energy: $$^{235}_{92}U + n \rightarrow ^{141}_{56}Ba + ^{92}_{36}Kr + 3n + \text{energy}$$ - The fragments have higher BE/A than uranium — the mass difference appears as ~200 MeV per fission.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (3m): Distinguish fission and fusion with one example each.** — Fission: heavy nucleus splits after neutron capture, e.g. ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n (~200 MeV). Fusion: light nuclei combine at ~10⁸ K, e.g. ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV. Both release energy as BE/A rises toward iron.
